message.content:
**Magnetic Field Calculation Using Ampère’s Law**

Ampère’s law for an infinite straight conductor gives the magnitude of the magnetic field \(B\) at a perpendicular distance \(r\) from the wire as  

\[
B=\frac{\mu_0\,I}{2\pi r}
\]

where  
\( \displaystyle \mu_{0}=4\pi\times10^{-7}\,\text{H·m}^{-1}\) (the permeability of free space),  
\(I\) is the steady current through the wire, and  
\(r\) is the radial distance from the wire.

---

### Plugging in the numbers

| Symbol | Value |
|--------|-------|
| \(I\) | \(10~\mathrm{A}\) |
| \(r\) | \(0.01~\mathrm{m}\) |

Now evaluate:

\[
\begin{aligned}
B &= \frac{(4\pi\times10^{-7}\;\text{T·m/A})(10\;\text{A})}{2\pi(0.01\;\text{m})}\\[4pt]
&= \frac{4\pi\times10^{-6}}{0.02\pi}\\[4pt]
&= \frac{4\times10^{-6}}{0.02}\\[4pt]
&= 2\times10^{-4}\;\text{Tesla}.
\end{aligned}
\]

---

#### Result

The magnetic field at point P, located **0.01 m** away from a 10‑ampere straight conductor, is

\[
\boxed{B \approx 2.0\times10^{-4}\; \text{T}}
\] 

or equivalently **0.00020 tesla**.
